findings.message: This is an instance fix: the finding wasn't fixed, only re-described. `people` is still built only from `mine.status` and `teamWeek` rows, and both need a `time.week` row. So someone who logged nothing in the week is still left out instead of shown at 0 h with every working day so far missing. The tool description now says a missing person 'has no timesheet or isn't someone you may see'. That still mixes up 'logged nothing' and 'not visible', and `below` can never return the person who is furthest below. Fix: list the people the viewer may see (the same scope as `hoursVisibleTo`/teamWeek, over hr people). Show those with no week at 0 h, status null and missingDays set to every working day before today.
findings.scenario: Dinesh (Maya reports to him) logs nothing in 2026-W43. Maya asks 'Who is below 80% this week?' (`get_week_utilisation {below: 80}`). Dinesh isn't in the result, though he is at 0%, the lowest of anyone.

findings.message: Half of the previous finding is still open. Time still imports `@amax/leave/contracts` statically, and it still decides whether Leave is installed with `to_regclass('leave.request')` instead of `hasModule('leave')`. Only the README changed. A switched-off Leave keeps its tables, so Time still reads and adjusts by leave. The new 'without Leave' test drops the `leave` schema. That isn't the module being switched off, so it never covers the `hasModule` path. Fix: gate `leaveIn` and the `leaveVisibleTo` check on `hasModule('leave')`. Test with `AMAX_MODULES_DISABLED=leave` (or the registry without Leave), not by dropping the schema.
findings.scenario: With `AMAX_MODULES_DISABLED=leave` and the `leave` schema still in place, `get_week_utilisation` W42 still returns `leaveDays`/`adjustedTarget` and `leaveVisible: false` from a module that is switched off.

findings.message:
This is an instance fix. The backfill covers weeks that existed when the migration ran, but the query still reads a `week_id` with no `week_status` row as a draft. The previous finding asked for that case to be treated as unknown. A week can still lack a status row:
- a week submitted between the migration and the 072 handlers going live (the event is consumed by a worker with no `week_status` handler);
- a week whose status event was dead-lettered.
In both cases the week's hours that carry a `week_id` are silently dropped, while its rows with a null `week_id` still count. Fix: when a row has a `week_id` and no status row, report it as unknown (or flag the person's figure as incomplete) instead of excluding it as a draft.
findings.scenario: Kasun submits W44 while the old worker is still processing events. No `week_status` row is written. Maya then applies a change request to a W44 entry, so the copied row carries a `week_id`. The corrected hours vanish from Kasun's billable hours with no mark.

findings.message: The fix for the missing-status major is proven by one case only: an applied change request on W42. The finding named at least two paths that write a `week_id` into an old week's rows: a correction that raises the revision, and an Admin's locked log into an old approved week. There is also an approved week, as well as a submitted one. Fix: add a table-driven test over these variants that fails without migration 0004.
findings.scenario: Delete the backfill's `approved` rows only: the test still passes, because it covers only Kasun's W42 change request.

findings.message: `leaveVisibleTo` is a new export on Leave's contract and Reports and Time already use it. It has no contract test, and the Leave README has no note about it. The module standard asks for both.

`exactWeekHours` (used by My week) and the grouped sum in `weekUtilisation` (`utilisation.ts:51`) are two copies of the same exact-hours query. They agree today, but a change to one filter (for example, deleted or locked entries) would split My week from `get_week_utilisation` again. Fix: build one per-user query and use it in both places.

Reports' migration reads `time.week` directly. The standard says a module's migrations touch only its own schema, and cross-module reads go through the owner's contract. This ties Reports' schema to Time's table layout and gets around Time's data scope. Fix: seed `reports.week_status` through a Time contract read run as a system job (for example a one-off workflow or the handler's first run), not from SQL against another schema.
findings.scenario: Time renames or splits `time.week.status` (for example it adds a 'reopened' status, which Reports' check constraint rejects). The Reports migration then fails, or inserts wrong rows, during a deploy that changed only Time.

findings.message: Instance fix, and in fact not a fix: someone with no timesheet that week is still left out of the result. The change only rewrites the tool description, which now tells chat that a missing person 'has no timesheet or isn't someone you may see'. Chat still can't tell 'logged nothing' from 'not visible'. `weekUtilisation` still builds `people` only from `myWeek` (when `mine.status` is set) and `teamWeek` rows, so the viewer is dropped too when they have no week. Fix: list every person the viewer may see (the same 071 scope `teamWeek` applies, through hr/allocations). Show those with no `time.week` row at 0 h, against their target, with every working day so far in `missingDays`.
findings.scenario: Maya manages Dinesh. Dinesh logs nothing in 2026-W43, so there is no time.week row. Maya calls get_week_utilisation {week:'2026-W43', below:80}. Dinesh, at 0%, is missing from the list, and chat says he may not be visible to Maya, though she can see him.
